hero.lead: Freelance Unity developer specialised in gameplay, systems and networking. I turn a design intention into solid, readable mechanics that feel great to play.
projects.title: What I've built.
projects.lead: Networking, spells, rhythm, controllers, combat systems. For each project: what I actually did.
p.discosmos.desc: Synchronous network infrastructure and skill architecture for a competitive 3D MOBA built in two months.
p.discosmos.tagline: A 3D MOBA built in two months, where netcode makes all the difference.
p.discosmos.ctx: Discosmos is a competitive 3D MOBA built in two months in Unity with Photon. I set up the entire synchronous network infrastructure and the skill architecture, aiming for the lowest possible latency so every match stays fair and readable.
p.discosmos.c1: Synchronous netcode: connection, rooms, player management and game-state synchronisation with Photon.
p.discosmos.c2: Latency: optimisation and lag compensation to keep actions responsive between players.
p.discosmos.c3: Skill system: architecture of the characters' abilities, casting and applying effects, replicated over the network.
p.discosmos.c4: Extensible code: structured so the team can add skills without touching the network layer.
p.beat-strike.desc: High-precision mobile rhythm engine, main gameplay loop and a Unity tool to compose patterns.
p.beat-strike.tagline: A mobile rhythm game where every strike is played on the beat.
p.beat-strike.ctx: In Beat Strike the level scrolls, enemies show up and the player chains tempo-synced interactions to attack and dodge. I developed the rhythm engine, the main gameplay loop and a Unity tool (Capacity Tool) to compose patterns in real time.
p.beat-strike.c1: High-precision rhythm engine, designed to stay accurate on mobile.
p.beat-strike.c2: Capacity Tool: a Unity editor with a timeline (BPM, duration, interaction type: attack, up / down dodge…) that designers can use without touching code.
p.beat-strike.c3: Patterns per BPM: a library of attack and defence patterns, picked according to the level's tempo.
p.beat-strike.c4: Gameplay loop: level chunk sequencing, attack and defence phases, interaction spawning and combat triggering.
p.heroes-dawn.desc: Mobile-first management RPG in an alternate New York: board exploration, turn-based combat on an active timeline and HQ management. Playable Brooklyn campaign (v0.9.0).
p.heroes-dawn.tagline: A mobile RPG where every turn is read on a timeline.
p.heroes-dawn.ctx: Heroes Dawn is a mobile-first management RPG set in the Apex Universe, the shared universe of Studio N29's projects. A squad of meta-humans explores New York zone by zone: rolling dice across a board, fighting turn-based battles on an active timeline and managing their HQ between missions. The current build (v0.9.0) offers a playable Brooklyn campaign in four zones.
p.heroes-dawn.c1: Turn-based combat on an active timeline, with team synergy replacing the former combo system.
p.heroes-dawn.c2: Playable Brooklyn campaign: four zones (Red Hook, Brownsville, Coney Island, Dumbo and the bridge) with objectives, enemies and narration.
p.heroes-dawn.c3: Onboarding and progression: first-login flow (cinematic, narrative nickname, campaign), HQ quest tracking (main and side quests) and an account architecture ready for Supabase.
p.heroes-dawn.c4: Clean architecture: layered code with an MVP interface, a pure-C# domain package, VContainer, MessagePipe, UniTask and EditMode / PlayMode tests.
p.delight.desc: 3D character controller, state-machine enemy AI and audio architecture, on a Rubika group project.
p.delight.tagline: A 3D adventure built around a fluid controller and reactive enemies.
p.delight.ctx: Delight is a 3D adventure made in a group at Rubika, now completed. I architected the core game systems: character controller, enemy AI and audio. A migration to Unity 6 is under way so the project stays openable and usable.
p.delight.c2: Enemy AI driven by finite state machines (FSM), reactive to the player.
p.delight.c3: Audio architecture and integration of sound into gameplay.
p.delight.c4: 3D asset integration into the game systems.

about.title: Gameplay developer, trained at Rubika.
about.p1: I'm a Unity developer specialised in gameplay programming, systems and networking. I studied at Rubika (Supinfogame) in the Programming Bachelor, and I now work as a freelancer under the STUDIO N29 banner.
about.p2: I like mechanics that feel good in the hands: readable combat, a spell that responds at the right moment, networking you never notice. My experience also gave me full-stack web, LLM / AI and prompt-engineering skills.
about.p3: I fit into a team quickly, communicate clearly and like shipping code that others can pick up.
skills.title: What I can take on.
skills.1.d: Game mechanics, combat, spells and abilities, game loop, controls and game feel.
skills.2.d: Network architecture, state synchronisation, replicated actions and consistency between players.
skills.3.d: Unity tools for designers: pattern editors, custom inspectors, data-driven workflows.
skills.4.d: Managers, pooling, serialisation and data loading: clean code that scales.
skills.5.d: Back-end APIs, graph databases, LLM integration and prompt engineering.
skills.6.d: Git, cloud, 3D (Blender, Unreal) and collaboration with art and design teams.
journey.title: Where I come from.
journey.1.d: Built an AI-based back-end API on graph databases, and a narrative game in Unity that uses this API.
journey.2.d: Showcase website for used vehicles with an admin interface, and setup of the digital tools (cloud, invoicing, stock).
journey.3.d: Hardware and software maintenance, and a consumables tracking app based on QR-code scanning.
journey.4.d: Video game programming studies: gameplay, systems and networking.

p.sweet-courrier.desc: Cooperative arcade shooter: arcade physics, local multiplayer input and game feel.
p.sweet-courrier.tagline: A cooperative shooter where everything comes down to feel.
p.sweet-courrier.ctx: Sweet Courrier is a cooperative twin-stick arcade shooter. I focused on game feel: control responsiveness and dynamic interaction physics.
p.sweet-courrier.c1: Local multiplayer input: handling several controllers and players on the same screen.
p.sweet-courrier.c3: Game feel: responsive controls, visual feedback and play sensations.
p.heroes-dawn.c5: In-editor design tools (Unity windows) for items, skills, agents and narration, CSV export for design spreadsheets, and balancing tools (spreadsheet import and simulator).
p.heroes-dawn.c6: Production documentation: GDD, game-design specs, art direction, UI flows and a roadmap (Steam Early Access, then mobile) laid out before writing code.
reviews.title: What clients say.
reviews.role: Product Operations Lead, Chukker App LLC
reviews.quote: Strong all-round contribution across. Djason delivered the first draft of the match simulation algorithms, integrated RP Vision from the GDD with solid stabilisation and performance gains, and set up a clean Unity architecture, Git workflow and documentation. Djason was a reliable partner in production meetings, helping scope and split tasks clearly. Highly recommended for Unity game development.
